subject.title: [Feature]: First-class org/team deployment — workspace scaffolding, RBAC, and deployment manifests

question: Should OpenClaw pursue first-class org/team deployment in core, decompose it into security-scoped RFCs, or keep the supported pattern as separate gateways plus existing multi-agent/docs primitives?
rationale: The current code has partial primitives, but the requested RBAC and manifest surface would define a new trust and config boundary that automation should not choose.

options.title: Decompose Into Security-Scoped RFCs
options.body: Use this umbrella for product context, but make the next actionable work the narrower RBAC, tenant/session identity, manifest, and docs decisions with explicit upgrade and security proof.

options.title: Sponsor Full Core Org Deployment
options.body: Accept a larger core roadmap item for scaffold CLI, manifests, and RBAC, with owner review across gateway auth, sessions, config, docs, and migration surfaces.

options.title: Keep Current Separate-Boundary Pattern
options.body: Decline first-class org/team core support for now and direct users to multi-agent routing, per-sender tool policy, and separate gateways for hard trust boundaries.

recommendation.title: Decompose Into Security-Scoped RFCs
recommendation.body: Use this umbrella for product context, but make the next actionable work the narrower RBAC, tenant/session identity, manifest, and docs decisions with explicit upgrade and security proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The related maintainer-labeled conversation identity work is the closest product-boundary decision point for this umbrella.
